# Notely

A small team notes app. Next.js App Router + TypeScript + Tailwind.

- Users live in `src/lib/users.ts` as an in-memory list.

   and set the sign-out redirect to `http://localhost:3000/`.

   cookie password (`openssl rand -base64 32`).

Routes: `/sign-in`, `/sign-up` (redirect to AuthKit), `/auth/callback` (session
exchange), sign out is a server action on the dashboard.

## Develop

```bash
npm run dev
```
EOF

content.text:
I've added sign-in to Notely using **WorkOS AuthKit**: email + password, Google sign-in, and `/dashboard` blocked for signed-out visitors. The build and lint pass. With placeholder credentials, a request to `/dashboard` while signed out is redirected to WorkOS sign-in, and `/` still loads normally. I haven't run a full sign-in, because that needs a real WorkOS project.

**Why WorkOS:** Notely keeps its users in a list in memory and has no database. A hosted service means no password hashing, password reset or Google OAuth code to build and secure. WorkOS hosts the sign-in screens, and email + password and Google are switched on in its dashboard. It's free up to 1M monthly active users. Auth.js discourages email + password logins, and Better Auth would need a database first. I checked the provided `docs/workos.md` against the installed package (v4.6.2) before relying on it.

**What changed:**
- **`src/proxy.ts`**: refreshes the session on every request and sends signed-out visitors to sign in. Only `/`, `/sign-in`, `/sign-up` and `/auth/callback` are open to everyone, so any new page you add is protected by default.
- **`src/app/sign-in/route.ts` and `src/app/sign-up/route.ts`**: send the visitor to the WorkOS sign-in or sign-up screen.
- **`src/app/auth/callback/route.ts`**: finishes sign-in, records the user, and lands them on `/dashboard`.
- **`src/lib/users.ts`**:
  - `upsertUserFromAuth()` links a WorkOS account to a Notely user. It matches by WorkOS ID first, then by email, so the existing Ada and Grace records are kept; otherwise it creates a new user. I added an optional `authId` field to the user type for this.
  - `getCurrentUser()` now reads the real session instead of always returning the first user. It returns `undefined` when nobody is signed in.
  - New `requireUser()` sends signed-out visitors to sign in.
- **Dashboard**: uses `requireUser()` (a second check on top of the proxy) and has a Sign out button (`src/app/actions.ts`).
- **Home page**: the default Next.js starter page is replaced with Sign in / Sign up buttons, or a dashboard link if you're signed in. I also changed the page title to "Notely".
- **`.env.example`**: placeholder values for the four WorkOS variables. Your `.gitignore` already ignored all `.env*` files, so I added an exception to let this one be committed.
- **`README.md`**: setup steps for the WorkOS dashboard.

**Before it works for real, you need to:**
- Create a WorkOS project and turn on Email + Password and Google OAuth. WorkOS's test environment includes test Google credentials; production needs your own Google OAuth client.
- Add `http://localhost:3000/auth/callback` as a redirect URI in WorkOS.
- Copy `.env.example` to `.env.local` and fill it in.

**Things to know:**
- There is no separate "Continue with Google" button on the home page. Google sign-in appears on the WorkOS sign-in screen once it's enabled there.
- The user list is still in memory, so it resets when the server restarts. Users are re-created automatically the next time they load a page, but you'll want a database before production.

Nothing is committed yet.
